questions.q: What is a "constitution" in Constitutional AI?
options: A legal document filed with a regulator before deployment
A written set of principles, stated in natural language, that the model is trained to follow
A synonym for the reward model's weights
A fixed list of banned words the model cannot output
questions.explain: The constitution is an explicit, readable set of principles the model is trained against, rather than an implicit pattern inferred only from scattered human preference comparisons.

questions.q: What happens in the first, supervised stage of Constitutional AI training?
options: A reward model is trained directly on human preference comparisons
The model produces a response, critiques it against the constitution, and revises it, producing data used for supervised fine-tuning
The model is trained purely on internet text with no principles involved
Human labelers manually rewrite every model response
questions.explain: Stage one is a self-critique-and-revise loop: the model checks its own output against stated principles and produces a revision, and those revisions become supervised fine-tuning data.

questions.q: How does the reinforcement learning stage of Constitutional AI differ mechanically from ordinary RLHF?
options: It doesn't use a reward model at all
The preference judgments used to train the reward model come from an AI model applying the constitution, instead of from human raters
It skips reinforcement learning entirely and only uses supervised learning
It requires no reward signal because the constitution is the reward
questions.explain: The RL stage of Constitutional AI is structurally the same as RLHF's RL stage — a reward model trained on preference judgments, with the policy optimized against it. The source of the judgments is the only thing that changes.

questions.q: Which of the following is a genuine advantage Constitutional AI offers over ordinary RLHF, according to this lesson?
options: It removes the need for any reward model
It scales preference-labeling without a constant supply of human raters, and makes the standard being optimized toward transparent and readable
It guarantees the model's values are fully aligned with the constitution
It eliminates the possibility of reward hacking
questions.explain: The lesson names two real advantages: scalability of feedback generation, and transparency, since the standard is a document people can read rather than an implicit pattern in a reward model.

questions.q: According to the open critiques discussed in this lesson, does writing a constitution remove value judgments from the alignment process?
options: Yes — because the constitution is generated automatically with no human input
No — someone still decides which principles to include and how to weigh them when they conflict; the constitution makes that judgment visible, but doesn't remove it
Yes — because AI judges are value-neutral by construction
No — because Constitutional AI uses no written principles at all
questions.explain: The constitution's authors still make value choices in selecting and weighting principles. Writing those choices down makes them inspectable and discussable, but it does not eliminate the underlying judgment call.
